parsed.explanation: A trans visitor who is outed faces state custody exposure rather than mere disapproval: since March 2022 mass raids arbitrarily capture trans women into birth-sex ordinary prison with documented forcible hair-shaving, handcuffed punishment drills, denial of HIV care, and guard sexual/physical assault for effeminate presentation. Social hostility is extreme (85% in 2013 said attacking a trans person was acceptable), gangs target LGBT people, and police often refuse cooperation. One 2020 conviction of three officers for a trans woman's killing and hate-crime laws show occasional recourse, but no working custody protection, so severity after outing dominates.

entry_documents.exposure: No gender identity law or recognition; foreign visitor documents have no domestic alignment mechanism. Documented border refusal for mismatch: not documented.
entry_documents.protection: 2022 supreme court ordered name-law reform for gender identity, but legislature had enacted nothing as of 2023.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented border practice, but unaligned status is linked by rights groups to prison abuse and lack of accommodation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Since March 2022 exception regime, trans women arbitrarily captured in mass raids held in ordinary prison, no gender accommodation; documented hair-shaving, handcuffed sun punishment, denied HIV clinic, four-month unsupported detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A judge freed one woman after about four months finding arrest unsupported; another woman remains imprisoned.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest leads to police lockup then birth-sex prison where guards/soldiers target effeminate dress/behaviour with searches, theft, sexual and physical assault.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational facility regime documented. National prison rules explicitly forbid effeminate dressing/behaviour and punish it; hospital ward placement: not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Capital-scoped cases only; no regional comparison, so national prison practice governs the documented visitor-relevant exposure.

care_services.exposure: Specialists dismiss trans patients' problems as being transgender, longer waits or denied care; hormone/surgery access severely restricted, lack of protocols/programmes.
care_services.protection: 2009 health ministry guidelines and HIV plan prohibit sexual-orientation discrimination in health services.
care_services.interaction: Custodial denial of HIV clinic shows guidelines do not protect detained trans women in practice.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2015 hate-crime provisions and 30-60 year bias-killing penalty exist, but police show blatant refusal to cooperate in LGBT death investigations and international reports find failure to address violence/discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 capital judge convicted three police officers, 20 years each, first homicide conviction for killing a trans person.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Paper protections coexist with mass-raid enforcement and prison targeting; the single conviction does not document systemic remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: No traveller-specific minor rule documented. Resident material notes families may expel LGBT children or use conversion therapy, not a visitor exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No evidence on guardian/parent treatment at border, custody or care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2013 study: 62% do not accept homosexuality, 85% believe attacking a transgender person acceptable; gangs target LGBT people with assault, sexual assault, forced recruitment, extortion; about 500 LGBT hate crimes 1998-2015, many unreported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2018 policy allows complaints against discrimination; one hate-crime homicide prosecution succeeded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public hostility plus thin police cooperation means street violence has no reliable remedy despite the isolated conviction.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether 2015 penalty framework produced further convictions is not sourced; homicide dataset figures 2000-2020 not itemised; no regional breakdown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Complaint policy and one working prosecution/ release by judge show some courts can act.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns do not offset documented birth-sex custody abuse and mass-raid detention, which recur without documented systemic remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar custodial beatings/assault, illusory remedies and months of unsupported detention, but this dossier lacks documented routine arrest for presentation, compelled confessions, or a capital provision; one police-killer conviction is a stronger remedy than in 0.15-A, so higher.

Very similar: birth-sex prison blocks with frequent assault, slow remedies, short/non-capital sentences. This case adds mass-raid arbitrary capture, sexual assault by guards for effeminate behaviour, and 85% attack-acceptance, so at or slightly below 0.25.

Higher severity than 0.35-A, where consequence is exclusion/humiliation without imprisonment. Here outing can lead to months in prison with documented custodial abuse and medical denial, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: hate-crime law and one exemplary conviction are outweighed by operative exception-regime policing, birth-sex custody, guard targeting of effeminate presentation, and extreme social hostility with police non-cooperation. For a visitor, discovery risks arbitrary detention and prison abuse with no gender-identity accommodation; health discrimination and gang extortion add everyday exposure. No execution or routine presentation-arrest statute is documented, keeping it above 0.15, but recurrent state custody abuse keeps it near 0.22.
